name: little-window-tab
description: Regression probe. little-window-hotkey already proves the chord opens a SECOND WINDOW; it never checked what is inside it, and what was inside it was nothing - CreateLittleWindow collapsed an invalid seed GURL to an empty startup_url, which the ctor reads as CreateWindowSlot's deliberate Cmd+N 'zero tabs' convention rather than the about:blank/default-page fallback its own comment promised. This scenario asserts the TAB, not the window: a little window opened via Cmd+Opt+N must add a tab and commit a real page (kLittleWindowDefaultURL, https://example.com) in it. A window-count assertion alone cannot tell a tab-less window from a populated one - that gap is exactly what let that defect ship.

actions.note: gate: AddTab logs unconditionally (little_ only changes whether the tab enters the Swift space pipeline afterward) - so a tab-less little window, the exact defect, would time out here instead of producing a false pass downstream. Hardcoded to id 2, not '[0-9]+': the fixture's startup space restores exactly one tab (id 1) before the hotkey fires, so id 2 is deterministically the little window's own tab, never the startup window's.

asserts a real http(s) scheme rather than a named host. What this scenario needs to prove is that a little window commits a REAL page and not about:blank - naming example.com adds nothing to that and tied the gate to a host the probe VM is not meant to reach. The url it commits is kLittleWindowDefaultURL, a constexpr in atrium_browser_controller.cc, so no fixture edit could have repointed it.

assertions.desc: one startup window plus the little one, same measurement little-window-hotkey uses

assertions.label: little-tab-added
assertions.note: restates the gate as a post-hoc assertion so a run that reaches quit without ever having added a tab is a reportable FAIL, not just a timed-out action

assertions.label: little-tab-committed
